deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the surrounding pages). X is a space stratified by a closed stratum Y with open complement X*. U*_{Y,X} is the deleted tubular neighbourhood (the 'link'), with maps p: U* → Y and j: U* → X*. Grothendieck considers the topos F of 'systems (17)': local systems on the three pieces together with gluing maps. He claims (22) that F ≃ Ĉ, presheaves on a category C. C is the collage, i.e. the Grothendieck construction, of the span of fundamental groupoids B = π1(Y) ← A = π1(U*) → C = π1(X*). Its objects are the union of the objects of A, B and C. Its arrows are those of the three groupoids plus arrows a→b, defined as arrows p_*(a)→b in B, and a→c, defined as arrows j_*(a)→c in C. The question being tested is whether F, which 'remembers' the π1 of the pieces, recovers the homotopy type of X when the pieces are K(π,1)'s.

This page, first example (X = C). The local group D = π1(U*) is the group of automorphisms of a. The notation 'I = D' (inertia = decomposition group) echoes the arithmetic/anabelian analogy. The only other non-identity arrow is a single arrow a→b, so b is a final object of C. A category with a final object has contractible nerve, and the classifying topos Ĉ has the homotopy type of the nerve. Hence F is homotopically trivial, matching X = C.

This page, second example. X = P^1_C ≃ S^2, Y = {∞}, X* = C, U* = D*_∞. Diagram (7) becomes the square (23): D*_∞ → D_∞, D*_∞ → C, whose amalgamated sum is S^2, not trivial. On the π1 side (next page) the span is Z → 1, Z → 1.

Grothendieck's conclusion (next page). He asserts C ≃ (• → •), which has a final object, so F is trivial while X is not. He infers that F does not in general give the homotopy type of X even when the pieces are K(π,1)'s, and that the canonical map (24) X → F need not be a homotopy equivalence.
errors: The computation of C in the P^1 example appears wrong. By Grothendieck's own definition of C (previous page), the span 1 ← Z → 1 gives a category with three objects a, b, c, Aut(a) = Z, and one arrow a→b and one arrow a→c. This category has no final object.
The nerve of that category is the homotopy pushout pt ← BZ → pt = ΣS^1 = S^2, by Thomason's hocolim theorem (1979). This is exactly the homotopy type of X = P^1.

So F should have the homotopy type of S^2, not be trivial. The stated counterexample to 'F recovers X when the pieces are K(π,1)' does not hold. More generally, X ≃ hocolim(Y ← U* → X*), and with K(π,1) pieces the collage of fundamental groupoids models that hocolim. So (24) should be an equivalence in this situation.
The description C = (• → •) on the next page drops one of the two terminal objects and the Z-automorphisms of a.

In the first example, 'b final' requires C to have only the objects a and b (or X* identified with U*). If X* = C* were a third object, b would not be final, although C would still be contractible. The precise stratification used in example 1 is unclear from the page.

ideas.what: Topos of 'systems' of local systems on strata and link, presented as presheaves on the collage (Grothendieck construction) of the span of fundamental groupoids π1(Y) ← π1(U*) → π1(X*)
ideas.modern_name: Exit-path / stratified fundamental category; constructible sheaves as representations of the exit-path category
ideas.usually_credited_to: MacPherson (unpublished, 1990s); Treumann (2009); Lurie (Higher Algebra, Appendix A); Ayala–Francis–Tanaka
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) sketches 'tame topology' and dévissage of stratified structures but not this explicit category

ideas.what: Homotopy type of a presheaf topos equals the nerve; a category with a final object is contractible
ideas.modern_name: Classifying topos of a small category / Quillen Theorem A-type facts

ideas.what: Test of whether the π1-data of the pieces (strata, link) of a stratified space determines its homotopy type, with P^1 = C ∪ D_∞ as test case
ideas.modern_name: Van Kampen / homotopy pushout decomposition; Thomason's theorem hocolim N(F) ≃ N(∫F)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Thomason 1979; Seifert–van Kampen; Brown (groupoid van Kampen)

ideas.what: Notation I = D (inertia = decomposition group) for the local fundamental group of the punctured tubular neighbourhood
ideas.modern_name: Topological analogue of decomposition and inertia groups (anabelian dictionary)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme; letter to Faltings (1983)

missed.claim: Grothendieck draws a negative conclusion: the topos of systems need not recover the homotopy type even with K(π,1) pieces. This rests on a miscomputation. With his own definition of C, the P^1 example gives S^2, consistent with Thomason. The record of this manuscript should note that the claimed counterexample fails, unless a later page corrects it.
missed.quote: on a maintenant une équivalence de topos T ≃ Ĉ, où C est la catégorie • → •, qui a un objet final — donc F est encore homotopiquement trivial, alors que cette fois-ci X ne l'est pas!
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historians reading the 1981 stratified-topos notes as anticipating exit-path categories should know that this specific negative claim is erroneous. The correct statement (collage of π1-groupoids ≃ hocolim) supports rather than refutes his program.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a routine worked example in an early sketch of exit-path-type categories for stratified spaces, which is itself a known later development (MacPherson/Treumann/Lurie). The only notable feature is an apparent error in the P^1 example that leads to a mistaken negative conclusion.
transcription_corrections: Previous page: the object set '{0,3}' is probably '{a,b,c}' (or '{a,b}'), the objects of the groupoids A, B, C.
'(ou contractile[?])' is uncertain; the handwriting suggests '(ou-...)', probably 'contractile' or 'ω-connexe'.
'X^* = [...] C': the struck-out word precedes ℂ; the reading X^* = ℂ is correct.
Last lines read 'Le topos F se décrit maintenant à l'aide des diagrammes correspondants sur les π1, à savoir'.
Next page: '$\mathbb{Z}^*_{2,2}$' is surely '$U^*_{Y,X}$'; the topos there written '$\mathcal{T}$' is the same F.
